stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Health agencies often estimate how widely measles is circulating from hospital admissions, because many infections are never reported. Before a vaccination campaign, the share of infections severe enough to require admission stays fairly stable, so admissions track infections closely. After a campaign, however, many of the infections that still occur are in vaccinated people, who seldom become seriously ill. Post-campaign admissions therefore ______ the number of infections that remain.
explanation: Follow the chain one step at a time. After a campaign, more of the remaining infections are in vaccinated people. Vaccinated people rarely become seriously ill, so fewer of those infections lead to a hospital stay. That means the admission count falls below the true number of infections. The blank needs a word for a count that comes out too low, and 'understate' is that word. Notice that the blank acts on the estimate. The admissions are a measurement, so they can understate infections, but they cannot change how many infections there are.

A.why: You carried over the first condition. Admissions track infections closely only before a campaign. 'However' tells you that relationship breaks down afterward, so admissions no longer mirror the true count.

B.why: You got the direction backwards. Vaccinated people who catch measles rarely end up in the hospital, so admissions miss infections rather than adding extra ones. The count comes out too low, not too high.

D.why: This is the subtype's trap: the right direction aimed at the wrong thing. You correctly saw that something gets smaller, but admissions are the measuring tool. They don't lower the number of infections. They make the number look lower than it really is.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When a city eliminated its rule requiring at least one parking space per new apartment, planners expected the number of spaces built to fall. It barely moved. Banks financing the projects judged that units without parking would be harder to rent, so they continued to require roughly one space per unit as a condition of their loans. The repeal thus ______ the parking requirement more than it removed it: the minimum now came from lenders rather than from the zoning code.
explanation: State the chain plainly. The city dropped its rule, but banks thought units without parking would be hard to rent, so they kept requiring about one space per unit. The minimum stayed about the same and simply came from somewhere else. The text after the colon spells this out: from lenders 'rather than from the zoning code.' A requirement that moves from one source to another has been relocated.

A.why: You finished the planners' expectation, which the passage knocks down. A repeal sounds like loosening, but the number of spaces 'barely moved' and the requirement stayed at roughly one per unit. This is the subtype's trap: you picked the direction the first step suggests and missed the second step.

B.why: You correctly saw that the requirement survived, then pushed it too far. The banks kept roughly the same one-space minimum. Nothing in the text says the requirement became stricter.

C.why: You noticed that lenders now impose a requirement but forgot that the city's rule is gone. A duplicate means two copies exist at once, and 'rather than' says only one source remains.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: People often assume that a plant closure drags down local wages, since laid-off workers flood the job market. A study of former mill towns complicates that picture. So many displaced workers moved away that the local labor pool shrank faster than the number of job openings did. Remaining employers therefore had to compete for the workers who stayed, and that competition ______ the wage cuts the closure might otherwise have produced.
explanation: Follow the chain one link at a time. Workers leave, so fewer workers are chasing each opening. Employers then have to compete for the workers who are left, and competing for workers pushes wages up. That pressure works against the cuts the closure would have caused, so it stopped them before they happened. 'Forestalled' means prevented in advance. The phrase 'might otherwise have produced' tells you the cuts never actually came.

A.why: You finished the first chain, where a closure leads to wage cuts, and never reached the second one. The competition among employers works against the cuts. It doesn't bring them on.

B.why: You picked a verb that points the right general way but acts on the wrong thing. 'Masked' means the cuts happened and were hidden. 'Might otherwise have produced' says they never happened, so there was nothing to hide.

D.why: Nothing in the text says competition made wage cuts look justified. That is a different kind of effect, one about how acceptable the cuts seemed, not whether they happened. The passage never supports it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For centuries, purple cloth signaled wealth because its dye came from thousands of crushed sea snails per garment. When chemists in the 1850s produced a synthetic purple from coal tar, the color became cheap enough to sell in bulk, and it soon appeared on market stalls as well as in drawing rooms. This abundance ______ purple's long association with rank: a mark that anyone can wear no longer sets anyone apart.
explanation: The chain goes like this. Purple gets cheap, so everyone wears it, so it stops marking anyone out. The colon backs this up with 'no longer sets anyone apart'. What gets weaker here is purple's link to rank, not the color itself. Something that wears away gradually has been 'eroded'.

A.why: This is the trap. Abundance really did make purple popular, so the verb points the right way, but it acts on the wrong thing. The object of the verb is the color's link to rank, and that link got weaker, not more popular.

C.why: 'Disguised' would mean the link to rank was still there but hidden. The colon says purple no longer sets anyone apart, so the link was actually lost. It wasn't hidden.

D.why: You got the direction backwards. Making the link official would make it stronger, but the passage says cheap purple stopped setting anyone apart.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: In drypoint, an artist scratches a copper plate with a needle, throwing up a rough ridge of metal, the burr, that catches extra ink and gives the lines their velvety blur. The pressure of the press flattens the burr a little with each impression, so later prints look thinner. Printmakers who want larger editions therefore coat the plate in a thin layer of hard steel, which ______ that flattening without altering the lines themselves.
explanation: The press flattens the burr, and a flatter burr makes fainter prints. The point of a larger edition is to keep prints looking good for longer, so the steel coat has to slow the flattening down. 'Retards' means slows, which completes the chain.

A.why: You got the direction backwards. If the flattening sped up, prints would fade sooner and the edition would get smaller, which is the opposite of why printmakers add the coating.

B.why: This is the trap. The verb points the right general way but acts on the wrong thing. Hiding the flattening wouldn't keep the burr holding ink, and the prints would still fade.

D.why: The coating doesn't copy the flattening. Copying it would be a different kind of effect, and it wouldn't explain how the coat makes larger editions possible.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Farmers who plant clover between cash-crop seasons are often advised to cut their fertilizer applications the following spring. Clover hosts root bacteria that draw nitrogen from the air and fix it in the soil, so a field coming out of clover has already been ______. Adding a full dose of fertilizer on top of that supplies more nitrogen than the next crop can absorb, and the surplus washes into nearby streams.
explanation: The bacteria add nitrogen to the soil. That explains the advice to cut fertilizer: the field already has nitrogen, so a full dose leaves a surplus that washes into streams. A field that has had nitrogen added has been 'enriched'.

A.why: You brought in the general idea that crops use up soil nutrients and got the direction backwards. If the field were depleted, a full dose of fertilizer would be needed, and there would be no surplus.

B.why: Nothing in the text says the clover protects the field. That is a different kind of effect, and it doesn't explain why extra fertilizer ends up as a surplus.

D.why: This is the topic-match trap. Roots may well loosen soil, but that is a physical effect. The sentence needs a reason the next crop already has enough nitrogen.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: On the Mercator projection, lines of longitude are drawn parallel rather than meeting at the poles, so east-west distances are stretched more the farther a place lies from the equator. To keep local shapes accurate, the mapmaker stretches north-south distances by the same amount. This choice keeps the outlines of coastlines faithful but thereby ______ the areas of high-latitude landmasses, which is why Greenland can appear nearly as large as Africa.
explanation: This chain has two steps. Places far from the equator get stretched in both directions. Stretching both ways by the same amount keeps their shapes but makes their area bigger. Greenland looking almost as big as Africa confirms that size is overstated. 'Inflates' means makes larger.

B.why: You got the direction backwards. Stretching makes places look bigger, and the Greenland example shows exactly that.

C.why: This is the trap. You saw that the map distorts something but picked the wrong thing. The passage says shapes stay accurate and coastlines stay faithful. Area is what gets distorted.

D.why: The passage is about stretching, which changes size. Nothing says landmasses end up in the wrong place, so this describes a different kind of effect.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Older keyboard tunings made a few keys sound sweetly pure at the cost of making distant keys grate, so composers mostly avoided those distant keys. Equal temperament took a different approach: it spread a small impurity evenly across every interval, so that no key was perfectly in tune but none sounded noticeably worse than any other. Because a composer could now travel to any key without arriving somewhere harsh, the system ______ modulation into remote keys.
explanation: Distant keys used to sound harsh, so composers avoided them. Equal temperament took the harshness away, so composers could use them freely. You need a word meaning 'permitted', and 'licensed' has exactly that sense here. It is a common word in an uncommon sense.

B.why: You got the direction backwards. Discouraging distant keys describes the older tunings. Equal temperament removed the reason composers had for avoiding them.

C.why: This is the trap. You grasped that the system improved things, then pinned the improvement on the wrong thing. The passage says no key was perfectly in tune, so nothing was purified. What changed was what composers could do.

D.why: The passage never says moving between keys became more dramatic. It says it became easier because no key sounded worse than another. That is a different effect from the one the text gives.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Researchers long assumed that island rails lost the power of flight simply because they had no predators to escape. But the absence of predators would only have made wings unnecessary, not costly. The decisive factor, one team argues, was the islands' scarce food supply, which made the energy spent building and maintaining large flight muscles a real burden and thus ______ birds with smaller wings.
explanation: Food is scarce, so large flight muscles become an energy burden. Birds that carry less of that burden do better, and those are the ones with smaller wings. 'Thus' tells you the blank follows from the burden falling on large wings, so natural selection 'favored' the small-winged birds.

B.why: You made the second step go the wrong way. The burden falls on birds with large flight muscles. Birds with smaller wings escape it, so they gain an advantage.

C.why: Wing size here has to do with energy cost, not with being seen. Hiding the birds is a different kind of effect, and the passage even says there were no predators to hide from.

D.why: This is the trap. You saw that scarce food matters but applied it to the wrong birds. Scarcity weighs most on birds feeding large muscles, so the small-winged birds would be the last to starve.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because fresh snow reflects most incoming sunlight back to space, the ground beneath a snowpack absorbs little warmth, and the air above it stays cold. An early-season snowfall can thus ______ itself: the chill it creates slows its own melting and makes it likelier that later storms will bring snow rather than rain.
explanation: Snow reflects sunlight, the air stays cold, and the cold slows melting and brings more snow. The text after the colon shows the snow keeping itself going, both by lasting longer and by causing more snow to fall. 'Perpetuate' means cause something to continue.

B.why: You got the direction backwards. The chill slows melting, so the snow strengthens its own staying power. It doesn't weaken it.

C.why: This is the trap. Later snow does follow, so the word seems to point the right way, but it names the wrong relationship. The early snow causes the later snow by keeping the air cold. It doesn't merely signal that it's coming.

D.why: Nothing in the text has the snow toning itself down. 'Moderate' doesn't describe the effect after the colon, where the snow lasts longer and brings more snow.
